Optimize 92 antipodal lines with absolute-value softmax annealing from paired-record and random starts, then expand to 184 points, break symmetry with full-code annealing, and LP-polish once.
direction: Search the centrally symmetric subproblem by optimizing only 92 antipodal representatives \(Y\), forming the 184 points \([Y;-Y]\), so the objective becomes minimizing \(\max_{k<\ell}|\langle y_k,y_\ell\rangle|\); initialize \(Y\) both randomly and by greedily pairing each record point with the point having the most negative inner product with it and taking the normalized difference as the representative. Optimize this reduced 92-line Grassmann packing with a smooth softmax over \(|\langle y_k,y_\ell\rangle|\), using tangent-projected gradient steps and an increasing \(\alpha\) schedule, then duplicate the result antipodally, release the antipodal constraint, refine all 184 points, and LP-polish once—allowing the released configuration to break symmetry after entering a different basin.

direction: Replace repeated LP polishing during search with many short, strictly budgeted equimax optimizations aimed at eliminating rattlers: parametrize points in local tangent coordinates \(x_i=\mathrm{normalize}(x_i^0+B_i u_i)\), where \(B_i\) is an \(8\times7\) basis for \(x_i^{0\perp}\), and use `scipy.optimize.minimize(method="L-BFGS-B")` with the analytic gradient of a staged log-sum-exp objective over pair cosines plus a penalty on the variance of the smooth per-point maxima \(M_i\), rebuilding the tangent bases after each outer stage and increasing \(\alpha\) through \(80,200,500\). Run diverse random/Sobol and record-perturbed starts for at most about 8 seconds each, discard candidates still above \(0.502\) after the first stage, enforce a global 155-second cutoff inside the callback, and give only the single best distinct candidate a final 20–25s LP polish.

idea: Large contact-graph surgery removing 12-24 jammed points and reinserting into refined spherical holes with periodic softmax annealing, keeping only improving basins before a capped final LP polish.
direction: Perform much larger contact-graph surgery than relocating one or two points: compute contacts at tolerance \(10^{-7}\), remove sets of 12, 16, 20, and 24 points chosen from the rattler, highest-degree hubs, endpoints of the tightest pairs, and random members of the low-contact block, then reinsert them one at a time into largest spherical holes found from at least 8,192 random sphere samples followed by 120 steps of single-point hole refinement against the currently fixed points. idea: Start from the exact E8 kissing configuration and greedily delete to 184 points with randomized tie-breaking, then softmax anneal in a new algebraic basin before a single time-capped trust-region LP polish.
direction: Start from an exact \(E_8\) kissing configuration instead of `best.npy`: generate the 240 normalized \(E_8\) roots—112 permutations of \((\pm1,\pm1,0^6)/\sqrt2\) and 128 vectors \((\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)/(2\sqrt2)\) with an even number of minus signs—then greedily delete 56 roots to obtain 184 points, repeatedly deleting a highest-degree root at cosine \(>0.499\) with randomized tie-breaking to preserve contact balance. Try about 20 deletion seeds, refine each briefly with softmax annealing (\(\alpha=50\to250\), roughly 150 steps), retain the best few, release all coordinates, and finish with one time-capped LP polish; this begins at cosine exactly \(0.5\) in a genuinely different, algebraically structured basin.

idea: Balanced-basin hopping that ejects overloaded hubs and rattlers into sampled spherical voids then reconverges with fast annealed softmax repulsion, saving a single capped trust-region LP for final tightening.

Degree-balanced surgery removing the rattler plus greedily-chosen high-degree hubs to delete maximal contacts, reinserting into 50k-sampled spherical holes with local then global annealing and LP polishing the top two.
direction: Perform degree-balanced contact-graph surgery that deliberately removes enough constraints to create a genuinely different basin: identify the rattler, points with at most four contacts, and greedy clusters of points with at least 22 contacts; for each removal size \(k\in\{1,2,3,4,6,8\}\), remove combinations consisting of the rattler plus high-degree points chosen to maximize the number of active contacts eliminated per removed point, then reinsert the removed points one at a time into the largest spherical holes found from at least 50,000 random samples followed by single-point softmax refinement. After each insertion, first optimize only the reinserted points and existing points with cosine above \(0.35\) to them, holding the rest fixed, then run a short global Adam/softmax anneal and reserve LP polishing for the best two surgical candidates; this directly attacks the isostatic jam instead of randomly shaking points that remain trapped by hundreds of other contacts.

idea: Delete 56 vectors from the 240 E8 minimal vectors by greedy max-contact removal with random tie-breaking, anneal each subset with log-sum-exp repulsion from p=8 to p=128, then LP-tighten only the best subset.
direction: Build a fresh, structurally symmetric seed independently of the record by starting from the 240 minimal vectors of \(E_8\): all permutations of \((\pm1,\pm1,0,0,0,0,0,0)/\sqrt2\) and all \((\pm \tfrac12,\ldots,\pm \tfrac12)\) vectors with an even number of minus signs. Greedily delete 56 vectors, repeatedly removing one whose deletion most reduces the number of pairs at cosine \(0.5\), with random tie-breaking over at least 20 deletion runs, to obtain diverse 184-point subsets; then relax each subset with a \(p\)-norm or log-sum-exp objective annealed from \(p=8\) to \(p=128\), followed by LP only for the best subset. This explores the balanced, orbit-like contact structures missing from the current asymmetric jam rather than making another perturbation of the published configuration.

idea: Target-feasibility continuation with sparse hinge Adam and violation-restricted kicks, polishing with trust-region LP only after beating the jammed optimum.
direction: Replace direct minimax descent by a target-feasibility continuation method: successively impose targets \(\tau=0.49997,0.49995,0.49992,0.49990,0.49985,0.49980\) and minimize the sparse hinge energy \(\sum_{i<j}\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau+0.002)^2\) using Adam on the sphere, retaining only pairs above \(\tau-0.02\) in the active set and updating that set every 20 iterations. If the energy reaches zero, continue to the next lower \(\tau\); if it stagnates, apply kicks restricted to endpoints of violated pairs and points participating in the largest LP dual stresses, then retry rather than returning immediately to the incumbent. Apply the trust-region LP only after a configuration first satisfies a target below \(0.49998295\), because feasibility at a prescribed lower threshold can change the active-contact topology in a way ordinary minimax polishing at the jam cannot.

idea: Large void surgery removing rattler plus hubs plus BFS cluster, sequential best-hole reinsertion with single-point softmax descent and frozen-core local plus short global anneal, accepting balanced topologies for one final LP.
direction: Perform large multi-point void surgery instead of 1–2 point relocation: each trial removes 14–22 points simultaneously chosen as (a) the rattler, (b) the 4 highest-degree hubs, and (c) a connected BFS cluster in the contact graph seeded at a hub (plus random variants), freezes the remaining $\ge162$ points, and reinserts the removed points one at a time at the best of 20,000 random sphere samples scored against all currently present points, refined by 100 steps of single-point softmax hole descent ($\alpha:60\to300$) before the next insertion. After all insertions, jointly refine only the moved points and their within-0.55 neighbours for 200 steps while keeping the frozen core fixed, then unfreeze for a short global anneal; accept only if the contact-degree variance drops and the max improves after a capped 20s final LP, with at most 8 such surgeries inside a strict 140s hopping budget—removing a whole overloaded cluster changes dozens of contacts at once, which single-rattler moves cannot.

idea: Sideways-walk hopping from the jammed code that keeps a walking state separate from the best, relocating low-contact/rattler points into sampled voids and kicking overloaded hubs, accepting small degradations to change contact topology, with cheap annealed repulsion reconvergence and one strictly time-boxed final LP.
Non-monotonic 5-member population with Procrustes and contact-hash tabu, fast softmax-Adam reconvergence and Metropolis acceptance, checkpointing and single final time-boxed LP polish.
direction: Use a strictly time-boxed, non-monotonic population search with topology tabu and anytime return: maintain five configurations separated by Procrustes-aligned RMS distance and by hashed contact graphs at tolerance \(10^{-4}\), optimize them with fast vectorized softmax-Adam rather than LP, and accept a worse offspring with a small Metropolis probability based on its smooth \(p=64\) energy so that alternative basins are not instantly discarded. Reject or penalize offspring whose contact-graph degree sequence matches a previously converged basin, checkpoint the best feasible array after every candidate, use an internal hard deadline of 150 seconds, and spend at most the final 20 seconds LP-polishing the single best distinct candidate before returning the checkpointed incumbent; this separates genuine basin exploration from both same-basin reconvergence and the timeout failures of previous programs.

Greedy E8-subset sampling with Gram-based deletion plus softmax reconvergence and single LP polish
direction: Restart from combinatorially distinct E8 subsets rather than perturbing the incumbent: generate the 240 E8 roots exactly (112 permutations of $(\pm1,\pm1,0^6)/\sqrt2$ and 128 vectors $(\pm\frac12)^8$ with even minus-sign parity), precompute their $240\times240$ Gram matrix once, and for 20–30 random seeds greedily delete 56 points by repeatedly removing a point with the most neighbours at cosine $\ge0.499$ (random tie-breaking, updated from the Gram matrix, no LP). Take the best few subsets, break the exact $0.5$ ties with a small group-agnostic tangential jitter (0.01–0.03), reconverge only with vectorised annealed softmax ($ \alpha:40\to320$, 300 steps) plus top-pair descent, and reserve a single 25s LP polish for the best candidate at the end, checking a 165s internal deadline throughout; this samples genuinely different contact graphs inherited from E8 instead of the incumbent basin.

idea: Flex escape along rigidity nullspace via eigendecomposition of contact Jacobian with global-rotation removal, large tangential steps and softmax reconvergence plus final LP polish.
direction: Escape along the rigidity nullspace of the active contact graph: from best.npy build the contact Jacobian for pairs within $10^{-6}$ of the max (project each point's gradient onto its 7D tangent space, giving an $\approx1100\times1288$ dense matrix), compute its SVD once (feasible in seconds), and take the smallest singular directions/null flexes after removing global rotations. Move with a moderately large step (tangential displacement norm 0.03–0.10 per moved point, i.e. far beyond the LP trust region) along random combinations of 5–20 flex directions—this preserves active contacts to first order while second-order curvature breaks/creates contacts—then immediately delete whichever contacts become violated most, reconverge with 200 steps of power-law repulsion, and only LP-polish candidates whose pre-LP max is below 0.5005; cycle 6–10 flex escapes and keep the best, so topology changes are driven by the actual jam geometry rather than random noise.

idea: Block-rebuild sideways hopping that jointly deletes jammed hubs and the loose low-contact block and greedily reinserts them into farthest voids, reconverging with fast softmax repulsion only and saving the trust-region LP for a single final polish to balance contacts and change topology.

Collective basin escape by deleting whole caps/clusters (18-point voids) and regrowing them with sequential farthest-hole insertion, then reconverging with cheap annealed softmax repulsion and sideways acceptance, saving a single capped trust-region LP for final polish.
